components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors

      title: Validation message

      type: object
      properties:
        message:

          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true

      properties:

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'

        email:

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature on `POST /api/owners` following the OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**What the change does:** when a create request sets `sharesHousehold: true`, the endpoint (as before) allows the owner even though another same-lastName owner exists at that address, and now additionally assigns a **stable, shared `householdId`** to every owner living together at that address, returning it on the owner.

**Files changed:**

1. **`AssignHousehold.java`** (new function) — computes `householdId` as a stable SHA-256-derived hex prefix of the normalized `lastName|address` (same normalization as `RequireUniqueHousehold`: trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, lower-cased). Because it's deterministic, every joiner at the same address gets the same value. It also back-fills existing household members that lack an id, so "both" sides share it.

2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted an `assignHousehold` step (with `govern: [ transaction ]`) between `assignCode` and `save`, so it runs on the built `Owner` before persistence.

3. **`Owner.java`** — added the `householdId` field/column (`household_id`) with getter/setter, so MapStruct maps it into `OwnerDto`.

4. **`openapi.yml`** — added `householdId` as a read-only field on the `Owner` schema (regenerates `OwnerDto`), documented as the shared household identifier. `sharesHousehold` was already present as a write-only input.

5. **Schema files** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added the `household_id` column to the `owners` table.

The acceptance test `coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` — which creates one base owner then two `sharesHousehold` joiners at the same lastName/address and asserts they return an identical, non-blank `householdId` — passes.
